answer: Each agent may propose trades, but its vote on prices is weighted by escrow: it must lock a scarce token that is forfeited if an independent auditor proves the agent fabricated counterparties or circular trades. A Sybil operator can create identities cheaply, yet splitting influence across them does not multiply voting weight; each added agent requires more tokens at risk and capital tied up until review. The plume of aliases may resemble a marble dune, but it cannot cheaply manufacture credible escrow.
